messages:
Maya (Sales): Hey team — Alex from Southwest Health is ready to kick off the Private deployment POC next week. They asked for a minimal egress/ingress checklist and exact ports/CIDRs to hand to their networking/firewall team. Can we compile?

Alex (Client): Yes, we need something we can drop into our change ticket. Primary ask: pinable egress IPs (we run strict outbound allowlist), and whether we need VPC peering or PrivateLink for control plane + model traffic. Also: any special ports for metrics/healthchecks.

Ravi (Solutions Eng): Quick summary: for Redwood Private hosted in a customer VPC we typically recommend either VPC Peering or TGW for L3 routing. PrivateLink is recommended when customers cannot accept route propagation or want interface endpoints. Tradeoffs: PrivateLink -> no route changes but needs ENIs & endpoint services; Peering/TGW -> simpler routing but you must manage routing tables. :information_source:

Joan (Network Eng): For the POC ask, we can provide two minimal configs. Both require outbound HTTPS to our control plane + model-serving endpoints. Ports: 443 (API/control plane), 80 (optional health probes if you choose HTTP), 22 (optional if you want SSH to bastion for debugging — not required), 50051 (gRPC serving if you use gRPC endpoints), 9100/9101 (optional Prometheus metrics if enabled).

Joan (Network Eng): Example firewall allowlist (customer side):
```
Allow TCP 443 to *.redwood-inference.com (we'll give explicit FQDNs/IP ranges)
Allow TCP 50051 to model-serving-private-endpoint.<region>.redwood-inference.com
Allow TCP 9100-9101 to metrics.<region>.redwood-inference.com (optional)
```

Ravi (Solutions Eng): About static egress: If you need a stable set of source IPs for outbound from our fleet, we support two options: 1) We provide a small set of stable EIPs if you run our gateway NAT in a dedicated account (requires procurement), or 2) You terminate outbound via your NAT/proxy so outbound to third-party services uses your static IPs. For the POC the fastest is to let us provide reachable hostnames and short-lived IPs; for production we'll lock down EIPs.

Priya (Security): From compliance side please note: if you will be sending PHI, TLS >=1.2 is required and customer must enable KMS for keying. Also we need the firewall to allow inbound only from our management CIDR for control-plane actions (we'll provide exact CIDR in the SOW). We'll also do an audit of allowed ports and limit SSH to timeboxed windows. :lock:

Alex (Client): Can you share the explicit CIDRs we should put into our ticket? We prefer CIDRs rather than FQDN rules.

Ravi (Solutions Eng): Sure — for the POC, use these placeholder CIDRs (we will replace with final ones after regen):
```
Control plane (management): 198.51.100.0/24
Model serving (region-us-west-2): 203.0.113.128/26
Metrics/observability: 198.51.101.0/24 (optional)
```
Note: these are placeholders — we'll publish the final list in the onboarding doc and rotate keys if needed.

Joan (Network Eng): Routing notes: if you choose VPC peering, add routes in your route table for the model-serving CIDR -> peering connection. If TGW, attach both VPCs and verify route propagation. For PrivateLink, create an Interface Endpoint in your VPC and update SGs to allow the endpoint ENIs.

Maya (Sales): Pricing/contract question from procurement: does Private (VPC) vs Dedicated capacity change the egress pricing model?

Ravi (Solutions Eng): Yes slight differences: Dedicated reserved capacity includes predictable throughput and a bundled baseline of outbound bandwidth; Private (customer-managed VPC) has the same per-token model but egress bandwidth typically sits on customer's bill if you route via customer VPC NAT. We'll loop in finance for exact numbers.

Priya (Security): Also clients often ask about firewall exceptions for healthchecks: we'll need inbound only from our monitoring CIDR for the port you expose (default 8080) — otherwise we won't be able to report liveness.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: POC staging env will be provisioned 2026-03-25 02:00 UTC — notify if you need a different window.

Alex (Client): Thanks. Two asks before we open the change ticket: 1) final, non-placeholder CIDRs for control plane and model-serving, 2) a single-page checklist for our firewall team (port, proto, direction, purpose). Can you deliver by EOD tomorrow?

Ravi (Solutions Eng): I'll draft the single-page checklist now and attach final CIDRs after the infra team finalizes EIP allocations. ETA EOD tomorrow — I'll post here when complete.

Joan (Network Eng): Action items:
- I will confirm final CIDRs and whether we can provide EIPs (by 1778460400).
- I will include recommended AWS SG rules and a sample route table snippet.

Maya (Sales): Great — I'll update procurement and cc Alex. Alex, we'll confirm kickoff after we post the checklist. :thumbsup:

Alex (Client): Sounds good — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maya (Sales): Closing thread for now, will append checklist + final CIDRs when available.
